land.text: Yi Province 'modern Sichuan and Chongqing' (Qiao Zong page) without Badong: the core round Chengdu, 'the capital of Yi Province'

predecessors.note: 'under the command of Mao Qu, the Jin governor of Yi Province'; soldiers mutinied in 405 and left Qiao Zong in charge. The western-jin dossier (loss 405) draws Yi Province as Sichuan plus Chongqing.

land.text: Yi Province, 'modern Sichuan and Chongqing' (Qiao Zong page); 'recovering Sichuan in 413' (Zhu Lingshi page)

successors.note: 'Qiao's state was destroyed by a campaign under military subordinates of Liu Yu in 413' (Qiao Zong page); Zhu Lingshi was appointed Inspector of Yi Province and recovered Sichuan in 413 (Zhu Lingshi page). Liu Yu's regime, the Jin court, is the successor; the Liu Song starts in 420.

capitals.name: Chengdu
capitals.note: 'set his capital at Chengdu, the capital of Yi Province'.

rulers.name: Qiao Zong (Prince of Chengdu 405, Prince of Shu 409)
rulers.note: Hanged himself after his cousin Qiao Daofu rebuked him, 413.

correction.text: Yi Province 'modern Sichuan and Chongqing' (Qiao Zong page) without Badong: the core round Chengdu, 'the capital of Yi Province'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a rebel state Cliopatria lacks. The page gives no area; Yi Province is 'modern Sichuan and Chongqing' and Badong (Chongqing) is gained in 410, so the core is Sichuan before that.

correction.text: Yi Province, 'modern Sichuan and Chongqing' (Qiao Zong page); 'recovering Sichuan in 413' (Zhu Lingshi page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'capture Badong Commandery' in 410 adds the Chongqing country to the Sichuan core, the whole of Yi Province (the western-jin dossier's 405-413 loss region).

region.text: Yi Province 'modern Sichuan and Chongqing' (Qiao Zong page) without Badong: the core round Chengdu, 'the capital of Yi Province'

ledger.note: 405: Qiao Zong seizes Yi Province. A mutiny of the soldiers of Mao Qu, the Jin governor of Yi Province, left him in charge; 'He proclaimed himself the Prince of Chengdu in 405.' The page gives no month.

409: Qiao Zong becomes Prince of Shu. 'In 409, Yao Xing created Qiao Zong the Prince of Shu' after he 'submitted as a vassal to Later Qin's emperor Yao Xing' around 407. The Later Qin dossier should carry the vassal_start (counterpart western-shu); its ledger has none.

410: Western Shu takes Badong. 'Qiao Zong then, after approval from Yao Xing, attacked Jing Province'; he 'withdrew back to his domain, but did manage to, in the process, capture Badong Commandery' (roughly modern Chongqing). Confidence 2: the page glosses Badong as the Chongqing area.

region.text: Yi Province, 'modern Sichuan and Chongqing' (Qiao Zong page); 'recovering Sichuan in 413' (Zhu Lingshi page)

ledger.note: Summer 413: Zhu Lingshi marches on Chengdu. 'Zhu did so in summer 413' after Liu Yu commissioned him with 20,000 men in 412; Qiao Daofu, set to defend the route, was beaten. The western-jin dossier dates its contest_start to late 412, the commission.

region.text: Yi Province, 'modern Sichuan and Chongqing' (Qiao Zong page); 'recovering Sichuan in 413' (Zhu Lingshi page)

ledger.note: 413: Chengdu abandoned. 'Qiao Zong... abandoned Chengdu and fled toward Qiao Daofu's camp'; 'Qiao Daofu... was captured and killed by Zhu'; the Zhu Lingshi page: 'Qiao Zong fled from Chengdu, allowing Zhu Lingshi to occupy the city.' No month on either page.

region.text: Yi Province, 'modern Sichuan and Chongqing' (Qiao Zong page); 'recovering Sichuan in 413' (Zhu Lingshi page)

ledger.note: 413: Western Shu ends. 'Qiao's state was destroyed by a campaign under military subordinates of Liu Yu in 413'; Qiao Zong hanged himself, his head sent to Zhu Lingshi. Land to the Jin court under Liu Yu (Zhu Lingshi 'recovering Sichuan in 413').

wars.name: Jin expeditions against Qiao Zong, 406-408
wars.outcome: Liu Yu's 406 attack was broken off when 'on the way, Sima Rongqi was assassinated'; Liu Jingxuan, sent in 407, 'advanced to Huanghu' in late 408 and withdrew; Qiao Daofu 'was able to resist Liu Jingxuan's advance'.
wars.note: No ground changed hands; Yao Xing of Later Qin was Qiao's suzerain from c. 407.

wars.name: Western Shu attack on Jing Province
wars.outcome: 'after approval from Yao Xing, attacked Jing Province'; withdrew but captured Badong Commandery.
wars.note: Jing Province (Jiangling, Hubei) was not taken.

wars.name: Zhu Lingshi's conquest of Western Shu

zones.text: Yi Province, 'modern Sichuan and Chongqing' (Qiao Zong page); 'recovering Sichuan in 413' (Zhu Lingshi page)

wars.outcome: Zhu Lingshi, commissioned in 412 with 20,000 men, took Chengdu in 413; Qiao Zong hanged himself; Yi Province returned to the Jin.
wars.note: 'recovering Sichuan in 413'; the Zhu Lingshi page lists Baxi, Zitong, Dangqu, Southern Hanzhong, Angu and Huaining under his later authority.

certainty.note: A rebel regime in a provincial capital: the pages name Yi Province and one commandery; no boundary.

sources.title: Qiao Zong
sources.note: Whole state: 405 proclamation, Later Qin vassalage c. 407 and 409, Jin expeditions 406-413, Badong 410, fall 413, capital Chengdu.

sources.title: Zhu Lingshi
sources.note: 413 recovery of Sichuan, Inspector of Yi Province, Qiao Zong's end; years only, no months.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; type rebel (a Jin governor's mutinous troops held Sichuan eight years); slug western-shu, the counterpart western-jin's ledger already uses (loss 405, contest 412-413, gain 413). Pages that failed: Mao Qu and Liu Jingxuan (URL_NOT_FOUND on the first try). The Qiao Zong page gives no month for the 405 mutiny. Unsettled: whether Badong (Chongqing) was Western Shu land from 405 (I drew Sichuan first and added Chongqing in 410, as the page does; western-jin draws Sichuan plus Chongqing from 405), and Western Shu's vassalage to Later Qin (c. 407 on the page, no end) which the later-qin dossier should carry. contest_start is summer 413 here against late 412 in western-jin.
